title: Lightweight SDK instrumentation: context weaver and loss-tolerant header adapter
creator: Maya Chen
description: Add a minimal-cost SDK instrumentation layer ("context weaver") that stitches request-level trace/context metadata into outbound requests across frameworks and languages. The adapter must be tolerant of missing or malformed incoming headers, provide sampling hint propagation, and avoid allocations in hot paths. Deliverations include: a language-agnostic header normalization spec, a Go middleware implementation, lightweight Node/TS helper, and runtime feature-flagging for gradual rollout.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes a single, documented middleware/hook API for Go and Node that can attach normalized context headers to outbound HTTP/gRPC requests
Header normalization spec published and linked from SDK README
Instrumentation adds <1% CPU overhead at 95th percentile in synthetic 1k RPS load test
Missing or corrupted incoming headers are handled gracefully and logged at debug level only
Sampling hint is propagated and honored by our local sampler (unit tests + integration)
Feature flag gating works and can toggle per-service via Console rollout
Automated tests for context round-trip and backward compatibility exist
Telemetry emitted: per-request attach latency, dropped-header count, and propagation success ratio
implementation_notes: Primary languages: Go (net/http + gRPC interceptors) and Node (express/axios / grpc-js wrappers)
Design as zero-copy on hot path: prefer header reuse and pooled byte buffers; avoid JSON allocations
Normalize header keys to lowercase and support dual-format carriers (single encoded header + legacy discrete headers)
Sampling hint precedence: explicit request-level > parent span hint > default sampler; record precedence in span.meta
If incoming trace identifiers are malformed, generate new trace and add provenance header with reason=malformed
Expose opt-in 'attachProvenance' flag to add signed 8-byte provenance stamp for higher-trust paths
Provide an adapter that can translate to/from OpenTelemetry baggage for downstream compatibility
Instrumentation should be idempotent (multiple middleware layers must not duplicate headers)
testing_plan: Unit tests for header normalization and sampler precedence in both Go and Node
Integration test: service A -> B -> C roundtrip verifying context preserved and sampling decisions consistent
Performance microbenchmarks measuring CPU and allocations per request at 95th/99th percentiles
Fault injection: corrupt incoming headers and assert system falls back and logs once per request id
Canary e2e in staging with real traffic shape and telemetry dashboards to validate propagation ratio
rollout_plan: Feature flag off by default; enable for observability-team services in canary pool (5%)
Monitor propagation success, attach latency, and error rates for 48 hours before increasing to 25%
After 7 days at 25% with no regressions, enable for core infra services and increase rollout to 100%
Provide quick rollback via Console feature toggle and pre-prepared remediation runbook
blockers: Need final sign-off on header normalization from platform-security
Consensus on provenance stamp format (8-byte vs 16-byte) pending research note
